description: Authored paraphrases of public NASA and NOAA educational pages; not sealed MPLPB evidence. No source images or full articles redistributed.

facts: Our solar system includes the Sun, eight planets, moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets.
It formed roughly 4.6 billion years ago from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.
Moons orbit planets, dwarf planets and even some asteroids.
Mercury and Venus have no moons.
Our solar system belongs to the Milky Way galaxy.
The Sun lies in the Orion Spur, a smaller arm between two larger spiral arms.
The Sun is a star whose gravity keeps the solar system together.
Its core is hot enough for nuclear fusion; the resulting pressure helps keep the star from collapsing.
Water moves among the atmosphere, land and underground stores, changing between liquid, vapor and ice.
Evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff connect those stores.
Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor when water absorbs energy.
Water can evaporate from a puddle or an ocean; plants also release water vapor through transpiration.
Condensation changes water vapor into liquid droplets.
It helps produce clouds and dew.
Ocean currents are movements of seawater driven by factors including wind, gravity and density differences.
Temperature and salt content affect water density; storms and earthquakes can also move ocean water.
